_README: RECONSTRUCTED FROM run-001, recorded in HANDOFF-run-001-failures.md.
Every endpoint, auth header, body shape and text_path below is what that
live run actually sent -- not written from memory. Seats 3 and 4 are the
two that WORKED. Seat 5 carries the temperature fix that run diagnosed.
Seats 1 and 2 failed with a cause the run did not record; diagnose-seats.py
settles them for well under a cent.
ONE INFERENCE, FLAGGED: the handoff records the Mistral and xAI hostnames
and says both are 'plain OpenAI-shaped chat completions', but not the URL
path. /v1/chat/completions is the conventional path for that shape.
Confirm both against the vendor page; the vendor wins.
THE OUTPUT CAP IS LEFT AT THE ADAPTER DEFAULT (4096) ON EVERY SEAT, AND
THAT IS DELIBERATE. A per-seat 'max_tokens' key would override it, and the
handoff flags two seats where 4096 may be too small: a reasoning model
spends thinking tokens from the SAME cap as the reply, so it can return a
well-formed 200 with empty text. But the cap also drives the pre-call
ceiling check, and raising it is NOT free. Measured on a 24-item
calibration, worst case across all five seats:
cap  4096  ->  $0.72   fits --max-cost 1.00
cap  6144  ->  $1.08   REFUSED at 1.00
cap  8192  ->  $1.43   REFUSED at 1.00
cap 16000  ->  $2.80   REFUSED at 1.00
So raising a cap without also raising --max-cost turns a seat that would
have answered into a run that never starts. If a seat reports 'cut off at
the 4096-token cap', add "max_tokens": <bigger> to THAT seat here and
raise --max-cost in proportion. Worst case scales linearly with the cap.
Those dollar figures are a deliberately conservative BOUND, not a forecast:
the estimator allows 5x the cap in billed output because reasoning tokens
are billed and are not bounded by max_tokens. Actual spend is normally far
below it. The ceiling refuses on the bound, which is the point.
Contains NO credentials. Keys live only in .env.
